item: the engine identity hashes the code index_article can reach in store.py instead of the whole file
summary: The engine id (R24 carry and backlog skip) hashed the BYTES of 24 files, store.py among them; store.py changed in 24 of ~40 commits that touched any engine file in the 30 days to 2026-11-02 (all others 0-7 each), so the id moved about every 18 h and a backup from another build almost never carried. code_digest now hashes, for store.py, the AST of the top-level definitions reachable (name-based, over-inclusive) from index_article plus every top-level statement, docstrings and comments excluded; every doubt (computed getattr, globals/eval/__import__, an import that is neither hashed on its own nor a non-repo package, a relative or self import, a redefinition, an unparsable file, another engine module importing the file by module) hashes the whole file as before. A one-time effect: every stamp made before this build is a different engine once. Measured on a 5,000-article plaintext restore-merge, same engine id on both sides: carried 10.7 s (467/s) against re-extracted 193.7 s (25.8/s), 18x; the cost of stamping them in the first place was 23/s. Pinned by tests/test_engine_identity_narrowed.py (every top-level function moves the id or does not, per the reachable set; constants, imports and top-level statements move it; docstrings, comments and line shifts do not; each fail-safe returns None). Limits: plaintext store; the gain exists only when exporter and importer share the output-relevant code, which the 30-day history says is the common case but is not measured on a real backup pair; an under-inclusion bug would carry a wrong row, which is why the walk is conservative.
